sources.cite: Edlow JA, Carpenter C, Akhter M, et al. Guidelines for reasonable and appropriate care in the emergency department 3 (GRACE-3): Acute dizziness and vertigo in the emergency department. Acad Emerg Med. 2023;30(5):442-486
sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case dizziness-central-red-flags, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 through the indexed abstract only (summarizing fetch): for acute dizziness under two weeks, HINTS by trained clinicians in patients with nystagmus; without nystagmus, the severity of gait unsteadiness helps tell central from peripheral causes; CT is not used for acute vestibular syndrome; MRI confirms central or equivocal HINTS findings. The full text was not read.

sources.cite: Hall CD, Herdman SJ, Whitney SL, et al. Vestibular rehabilitation for peripheral vestibular hypofunction: an updated clinical practice guideline from the Academy of Neurologic Physical Therapy of the APTA. J Neurol Phys Ther. 2022;46(2):118-177
sources.note: Relayed from the DPT case dizziness-central-red-flags, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 (first part of the guideline PDF, summarizing fetch with quotes): gaze stabilization 3 times a day for at least 12 minutes daily in acute or subacute unilateral hypofunction; the guideline 'may not apply to individuals with central vestibular disorders'; stopping when goals are met, symptoms resolve or progress plateaus. Journal and year are from the published citation, not from the fetched excerpt.
